newsitem.title: POLAND: GOLOTA GETS SUSPENDED JAIL TERM FOR 1990 BRAWL.
newsitem.headline: GOLOTA GETS SUSPENDED JAIL TERM FOR 1990 BRAWL.

text.p: A Polish court hit boxer Andrzej Golota with a suspended two-year jail term and a $7,000 fine on Thursday after he returned to his homeland to face the music over a restaurant brawl seven years ago.
Private Radio Zet said heavyweight Golota didn't flinch when the court in Wloclawek, central Poland passed the jail sentence, suspended for three years, but his wife Mariola sighed with relief.
Golota, 28, looks forward to a bright career in the United States, although he last year twice squandered likely victories against U.S. rival Riddick Bowe by landing low blows.

But he did not dare come home to Poland for years, because he was wanted by police over the May 1990 events in a Wloclawek restaurant, and finally decided to face a Polish court after getting official guarantees he would not face instant arrest.

Mariola Golota said they wanted to get back to the United States as fast as possible and Andrzej was planning new fights although he was still recovering from jaw injuries, from his last clash with Bowe, which made eating painful.
She said his next contest was likely in May, but did not specify with whom.

"I think the more timid (boxers) will try to wriggle out of fighting him, saying that he commits fouls and so on, but those who want to stay at the top will want to prove that they are better then this Pole," she said.
Golota was accused of beating a stranger, Pawel Bialostocki, and robbing him of his shirt, trousers and a shoe in a restaurant in Wloclawek, central Poland.

Golota expressed regret and apologised to Bialostocki in court, but argued that he had taken the man's clothes in the restaurant bathroom to ensure that he was paid for a shirt which Bialostocki had torn and not to keep them.
Despite the painful circumstances of his return, Golota got a hero's welcome in Poland and the court-room was surrounded by admirers.
